answer: A workable defence is stake-and-history identity: a new agent must lock a refundable deposit and earn trust only by completing small, checked jobs over weeks. Its reputation is a mirror of that verified record, not of how many accounts it claims. An attacker creating thousands of identities faces a karst-like problem: each fake account is another hollow to fill with its own deposit and slow history, so cost grows linearly while reward does not. Honest agents gather in a shared oasis of verified work, where one long-lived record is worth far more than a crowd of empty shells.
